item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
First off all there is censoring in the containment procedures. How should they be obeyed to if some parts are censored? And what is the point of ceeping the level of lockdown or the number of embedded agents secret?

Psssst… this article is 1548 days old, and was written in 2011. It's pretty old, so it's not consistent with current site standards because the author at the time would not have known that in the future, containment procedures would be expected to be uncensored. Remember to pay attention to how old an article is when reviewing it; you can (and should!) check article age by clicking the "History" link at the bottom of a page, and looking for the page creation date.

Edit: Of course, this doesn't factor into actual votes. If you like it, go ahead and upvote it.

Also, sometimes blackboxes are used as style points, to cover up numbers that leave it up to the reader to decide how many other experiments or documents there might be in existence, in the case of "Document 277-██".

And the rabits are called SCP-277-1-█R in the evacuation log, SCP-277-R█ in the part after the log and SCP-277-██ in the interview.

This is an issue. I'll get a staff member to take a look at it momentarily. Thanks for the heads up!

item.content:encoded:
I think this is a nice SCP, wich gets especially creepy with the interview. Although there are some things that bother me.

First off all there is censoring in the containment procedures. How should they be obeyed to if some parts are censored? And what is the point of ceeping the level of lockdown or the number of embedded agents secret?

Also there is a lot of censoring in the text that seems to be pointless and makes it hard to read. For example "Document 277-██". Its a list of children in a town under a lockdown, not a list of the real names of the O5 members. If its content has to be secret, it would have some access requirements, but its ID wouldn't need to be secret.

The log of OPERATION 277-██████ is so much censored, i had to read it twice to make a sense of it.

And the rabits are called SCP-277-1-█R in the evacuation log, SCP-277-R█ in the part after the log and SCP-277-██ in the interview. Also I don't get the point of censoring here.

I suggest asking yourself on everything censored: "Why should this be secret?" If you can't give youself an answer like "safety issues" or "O5-stuff" you might considder not censoring it.

Just thinking..

item.content:encoded:
From what I've read, saying what the various parts of the SCP are falls under the description category. Here's what I would put as the containment procedures:

Due to difficulty in containing SCP-277, it has been placed under a Level-█ lockdown. Activities of the citizens of SCP-277 and of SCP-277-1 must be monitored by no less than █ embedded agents, and civilians must not be aware of the Foundation or its involvement in monitoring SCP-277. Any attempts to contact civilians within SCP-277 by those outside SCP-277 must be investigated. Personnel must undergo psychological screening before being assigned to SCP-277.

The rest should be in the description, I think. Also, as a side note, we already have a city of missing persons, SCP-599. It could say that their information doesn't match anything on record, or something. Your call on that bit, really.

While I thought the interview was interesting and it did explain the second part of the article, it's not entirely necessary to expunge the fact that they were eating the sketches. It doesn't feel redaction worthy. Unless, of course, they're doing something worse, in which case you need to expunge a bit more so we can leave it up to our imaginations.

Feel free to disregard any of this; I don't think I have any more experience than you do.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Okay, here goes:

I like this one. I really do. It is a cool idea and you write well. However, I had to downvote for a few reasons.

First off, your tone is a bit off. Try making it more clinical.

"Civilians are aware of Foundation presence as well as our moderation of their activities, and have proven to be surprisingly compliant." I think you mean "monitoring." That's not a huge deal though.

In my opinion, if Area I-4 = SCP-277 then you don't really need to specify Area I-4. You can just call it SCP-277, since they are one and the same. It would be like saying "This is John Smith. Call him Bob Millers." Just an unnecessary level of complication.

Your use of [DATA EXPUNGED] and [REDACTED] is very sloppy, and makes this hard to read. A few times it is okay, but I feel as though you overuse them, and make sentences very very choppy. You really should only use them if either A) it is something the Foundation would actually block out or B) our imaginations will create a wonderful horror for us, far surpassing anything an author would write.

I really liked the interview log, but I don't like that it turns out to be one boy who is possessed or something. That was kind of a bummer for me, and made it too easy to explain; I liked it better when there were just random rabbits who ate kid's imaginations.

Overall, I feel like you just have too much going on here (part of the reason it is so damn long). I can really see this one working if you condense it a bit, maybe cut out the part about all the residents being missing persons (it just seemed a little random and unnecessary, but that's just me).

All that said, I am still relatively new to the site, so take all my advice with a grain of salt. Good luck!
